hard_failures: Flicker at 1.70s (frame 51): the silver light strip on the cap dims for one frame, then comes back. This is a visible single-frame luminance pop in the near-dark opening.

Specular blow-out flashes at 5.77-5.97s (frames 173-179) and 7.57-7.73s (frames 227-232): the left side face turns pure white with black droplet dots for 2-4 frames, then snaps back. Mean luma jumps 28->41->28 (largest frame-to-frame jump in the film). It reads as a strobe or white panel, not glass.

Particles cover the product: dark droplet speckles are spread over the whole glass body in every shot, including the 11-15s hero hold (and around the cap at 12-15s). The reference bottle is clean glass, and the brief bans particles over the product.
Audio clipping: about 11,600 decoded samples sit at or above full scale (peak 1.26), and the 9.0-9.2s impact window measures about -0.1 dBFS RMS. The bass hit will distort on phone speakers.
issues: 1.6-1.8s: find what drives the light-strip intensity at frame 51 (a keyframe step, a noise function or a light parameter jump) and make it a smooth eased curve. No single-frame dips.

5.7-6.0s and 7.5-7.8s: the side face blows out to white as the orbit crosses the key light's specular angle. Lower the side light's intensity or the env-map contribution, or raise roughness on the side bevel, so the side face peaks at mid-grey. Apply the same fix to the brief white strip on the top shoulder at 3.5-4.5s.

Whole film, worst at 11-15s: remove the droplets stuck to the glass or drastically thin them out. Keep suspended droplets only in the background or off to the sides during 3-7s, and fade them to zero by 10.5s so the hero bottle is clean black glass like the reference. Nothing should overlap the label, the cap or the body silhouette.

Cap (all shots): the vertical light bands make the brushed cap look fluted or faceted. Use a smooth cylinder with a horizontal brushed anisotropy and one soft vertical highlight, as in the reference's bottom-right view. Keep the fine groove ring near the cap base.

11-15s hero: the required silver rim light is barely there, and the body edges merge into the background. Add a cool white or silver back-rim from behind left and right, so there is a crisp thin outline on both vertical edges and the shoulders. Keep it hard-edged with no bloom.

9.0-10.5s mist: the mist is blotchy grey cloud puffs that take up the whole frame, not a fine wave. Use finer, lower-opacity mist in a directional band behind the bottle only, travelling outward from the 9.0s impact, and dissipate it fully by 11.0s.

8.6-8.7s: the push-in to the label close-up and the start of the pull-back produce several large frame-to-frame changes (luma diff around 10-11). Smooth the camera velocity through the turnaround and keep the 9.0s beat as the single accent.

Audio: put a limiter on the master bus with a -1 dBTP ceiling and pull the impact down about 4-6 dB so it peaks rather than sits at full scale. The impact onset is correctly at 9.00s (the largest dB rise and largest bass rise both start there), so keep the timing.

11.5-15s typography: the tagline 'SCENT. WITHOUT WORDS.' is thin and small at phone size (about 18px cap height at 1080w). Increase its size by about 25-30% or its weight and contrast slightly. The NOIR wordmark is good.
11-15s framing: the hero bottle takes up only about 56% of frame width and sits high. Consider bringing the camera about 10% closer so the product dominates the hold.
